candidates.change_summary: Delete the statement `require(msg.value == 10 ether);` so calls with any value are accepted and can change pastBlockTime/payout behavior.
Delete the statement `require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime);` so multiple calls in the same block are allowed, changing pastBlockTime outcomes.
Replace `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp + 1;` with `pastBlockTime = block.timestamp;` so same-timestamp calls in a later block pass the require differently than before.
Replace the payout condition `block.number % 15 == 0` with `block.number % 15 != 0` so payouts occur on different blocks.
Delete the `payable(msg.sender).transfer(...)` statement inside the if so the contract never pays out, changing observable balance/refund behavior.
Remove the requirement that msg.value equals 10 ether, allowing calls with any value to proceed.
Remove the requirement that block.timestamp be greater than pastBlockTime, allowing multiple calls in the same timeframe.
Set pastBlockTime to block.timestamp instead of block.timestamp + 1, changing the stored timestamp value and the timing window.
Remove the assignment updating pastBlockTime so it stays at its initial value forever.
Change the payout condition from block.number % 15 == 0 to block.number % 15 != 0, inverting which blocks trigger the transfer.
Change the payout condition to always true so every valid call triggers the transfer.
Delete the require that msg.value equals 10 ether, allowing any value to trigger the payout logic.
Delete the require that block.timestamp is greater than pastBlockTime, allowing multiple calls in the same timestamp window.
Replace the modulo divisor 15 with 16 so payouts occur on different block numbers.
Set pastBlockTime to block.timestamp instead of block.timestamp + 1, allowing a call in the immediately following second.
Delete the payout transfer so the contract never returns its balance to the caller.
Delete the require(msg.value == 10 ether) check so calls with any value are accepted and pastBlockTime updates.
Replace the timestamp guard with an inverted condition so every call reverts and pastBlockTime never changes.
Move the pastBlockTime assignment above the require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime) guard so the guard always fails and calls revert.
Replace the assignment with pastBlockTime = block.timestamp so the stored value differs by one second.
Delete the pastBlockTime assignment so the state variable is never updated by the fallback.
Invert the payout condition to block.number % 15 != 0, changing when transfers occur.
Delete the require that msg.value equals 10 ether so calls with any value proceed.
Change the time guard from strict inequality to non-strict inequality, allowing multiple calls in the same timestamp.
Set pastBlockTime to block.timestamp instead of block.timestamp + 1, changing which subsequent calls are accepted.
Delete the update of pastBlockTime so the one-call-per-block-time restriction no longer takes effect.
Change the payout condition from block.number % 15 == 0 to block.number % 15 == 1, altering when funds are transferred.
Transfer 0 instead of the contract balance on the payout branch.
